domain_label: Dental Exam & Licensure — INBDE Content and the Foreign-Trained (FMG) Pathway to US Dental Licensure
purpose: A method for an internationally trained (non-CODA) dentist and their advisor to reason about the single US dental knowledge board (the INBDE) and the full foreign-graduate licensure pathway: what the INBDE is and who owns it, how a non-CODA graduate becomes eligible (ECE credential evaluation + DENTPIN), the exam format/blueprint/scoring/retake rules, and the surrounding gates (ECE -> ADEA CAAPID -> a CODA advanced-standing DDS/DMD -> a separate regional clinical exam such as ADEX/DLOSCE -> state-by-state licensure), while carrying every unverified number (exact fees, retake interval, current pass rates, the full 56-item clinical-content enumeration, and the exact non-CODA-friendly state list) as a named [UNKNOWN]/[ESTIMATE] blocker rather than inventing it.
assumptions: no directly-read official JCNDE/ADA/ADEA/ECE page was available at compile time (jcnde.ada.org, ada.org, ece.org and university mirrors returned HTTP 403 under the session egress policy); facts were reconstructed from search-engine snippets of those official pages plus corroborating secondary aggregators, and every claim not confirmable against a directly-read official page is tagged [ESTIMATE] or [UNKNOWN]

the candidate is a foreign-trained (non-CODA/CDAC) general-dentistry graduate seeking full US licensure, for whom requirements are set per US jurisdiction (state board) so the exact combination varies by state
the INBDE is treated as a knowledge exam only; the separate hands-on clinical licensure exam and the state jurisprudence exam are distinct downstream gates named but not fully specified here
item counts, day timing, fee magnitudes and the retake interval are labeled estimates from secondary guides quoting the JCNDE Candidate Guide, not values read from a live official fee/candidate page

the 10 Foundation Knowledge areas are a high-confidence estimate corroborated across independent secondary sources; the full verbatim 56 Clinical Content enumeration with official numbering is an explicit UNKNOWN blocker, not reconstructed as fact
exclusions: the verbatim, officially numbered enumeration of all 56 Clinical Content areas (the JCNDE PDFs present them as figures/images and every direct fetch returned 403) — held as a named UNKNOWN, never invented
official per-FK or per-CC item-weight percentages beyond the 3-group counts/weights that secondary sources report, and any official current-cycle pass/fail statistics
the detailed content of the clinical (hands-on) exam procedures, manikin/CompeDont scoring rubrics and the periodontal/restorative skill criteria (named as a downstream gate only)
specialty-board (AEGD/GPR/orthodontics etc.) and residency-alternative licensure routes beyond noting that some states accept a PGY-1 residency in lieu of a clinical exam
any fabricated exam fee, retake interval, pass rate, program tuition, or state enumeration the research file did not verify

competency_questions.question: What is the INBDE, who owns and runs it, and what did it replace?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states INBDE = Integrated National Board Dental Examination, run by the Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations (JCNDE) under the ADA, launched Aug 2020 replacing NBDE Part I and Part II, and that it is a knowledge (computer-based) exam only

competency_questions.question: What three independent gates must a foreign-trained (non-CODA) dentist clear to be licensed as a US general dentist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer names the education gate (usually a CODA advanced-standing DDS/DMD), the credential-evaluation/exam-eligibility gate (ECE + DENTPIN + INBDE), and the clinical-exam gate (ADEX/DLOSCE), and states requirements are set per state board

competency_questions.question: How does a non-CODA graduate become eligible to sit the INBDE, and in what order do the steps happen?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states a JCNDE-designated ECE credential evaluation plus a DENTPIN are required, gives the DENTPIN -> ECE -> JCNDE eligibility email -> schedule INBDE sequence, and notes current non-CODA students additionally need a dean/registrar Certification of Eligibility [ESTIMATE]

competency_questions.question: What is the INBDE format — item count, day structure and timing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer gives ~500 multiple-choice items over 2 days (Day 1 ~8h/~360 items incl. some case-based, Day 2 ~4h/~140 all case-based) and tags the counts/timing as high-confidence estimate not read from a live Candidate Guide

competency_questions.question: What is the INBDE content blueprint and what makes it 'integrated'?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states the blueprint is a 10 Foundation Knowledge x 56 Clinical Content matrix where each item integrates >=1 FK applied within a CC area, lists the 10 FK areas [ESTIMATE], and gives the 3 CC groups with counts 13/23/20 and reported ~36.2/42.0/21.8% weights [ESTIMATE]

competency_questions.question: Why can the full 56 Clinical Content list not be stated authoritatively here, and how should that gap be handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer names the blocker (the JCNDE Item Development Guide / Domain of Dentistry PDFs present the 56 areas as figures and every direct fetch returned 403), marks the full verbatim numbered list UNKNOWN, and routes it to a fetch-enabled verification run rather than reconstructing it as fact

competency_questions.question: How is the INBDE scored and what is the pass rule?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states scaled score range 49-99 with a passing standard of 75 [FACT], pass/fail reporting with diagnostic FK/CC feedback for failers and no numeric score for passers, and that the passing standard was raised effective June 2024

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer gives the reported ~$890 INBDE fee and ~$435 non-CODA processing fee (2026) plus a separate ECE evaluation cost, all tagged [ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN] needing verification against the live Apply/fee page and marked non-refundable/non-transferable

competency_questions.question: How does a foreign-trained dentist close the education gap, and through what application service?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states most states require a CODA-accredited DDS/DMD, that foreign dentists close the gap via a ~2-3 year International Advanced Standing DDS/DMD program, and that ADEA CAAPID is the centralized application (cycle ~March-January) needing an ECE Course-by-Course report

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer names the ADEX exam (and DLOSCE), administered by CDCA-WREB-CITA and increasingly on manikins/CompeDont, and states only CODA/CDAC students/graduates may take ADEX directly while other international graduates must apply through a specific state board — a key reason to route through a CODA advanced-standing program

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer composes ECE eval + DENTPIN -> INBDE (pass 75) -> ADEA CAAPID -> CODA advanced-standing DDS/DMD -> ADEX/DLOSCE clinical exam -> state licensure (+ jurisprudence), and flags the fee, retake-interval, pass-rate, 56-CC-enumeration and non-CODA-state UNKNOWN blockers instead of asserting them

glossary.definition: Integrated National Board Dental Examination — the single computer-based knowledge board exam required across US licensing jurisdictions, launched August 2020 to replace NBDE Part I and Part II; 'integrated' because each item applies Foundation Knowledge within a Clinical Content area [FACT].

Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations — the agency operating under the American Dental Association (ADA) that owns and runs the INBDE and publishes its Candidate Guide, Item Development Guide, Domain of Dentistry model and Technical Report [FACT].

A dentist whose dental degree is from a school not accredited by the US Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA) or Canada's CDAC; in most US states this degree is by itself not accepted for full general-dentistry licensure, which drives the advanced-standing pathway [FACT].

Educational Credential Evaluators — the JCNDE-designated evaluator of foreign dental credentials; a U.S. General Report typically suffices for exam eligibility, while a Course-by-Course Report is what advanced-standing programs require [FACT]. It is a prerequisite for JCNDE to grant INBDE eligibility to a non-CODA candidate.

The ADA's personal identification number a candidate must obtain before credential evaluation and INBDE eligibility; the eligibility sequence is DENTPIN -> ECE evaluation sent to JCNDE -> JCNDE eligibility email -> schedule the INBDE [FACT for DENTPIN requirement; sequence part ESTIMATE].

The INBDE content matrix of 10 Foundation Knowledge (FK) areas by 56 Clinical Content (CC) areas; every item integrates at least one FK area applied within a CC area [FACT]. The 56 CC areas fall into 3 groups (Diagnosis & Treatment Planning, Oral Health Management, Practice & Profession).

The full verbatim, officially numbered list of all 56 Clinical Content areas; the JCNDE PDFs present them as figures/images and every direct fetch returned HTTP 403 under the session egress policy, so the complete list is an explicit UNKNOWN blocker to be verified against the Item Development Guide, never reconstructed as fact.

The INBDE reports a scaled score on a 49-99 range with a passing standard of 75 [FACT]; results are pass/fail (passers get no numeric score, failers get diagnostic FK/CC feedback), and the standard was raised effective June 2024, increasing failures [ESTIMATE on the effect size].

ADEA Centralized Application for Advanced Placement for International Dentists — the single application, cycle running ~March through January, to multiple CODA advanced-standing DDS/DMD programs; most programs require an ECE Course-by-Course report [FACT].

The ADEX Dental Examination is the dominant regional clinical (hands-on) licensure exam, developed by ABDE and administered by the merged CDCA-WREB-CITA, increasingly on manikins/CompeDont; the DLOSCE is the ADA's standardized non-patient clinical-judgment exam. Only CODA/CDAC students/graduates may take ADEX directly; other international graduates must apply through a specific state board [FACT].

nodes.definition: Frame the foreign-graduate route as THREE independent gates that all must be cleared, set per US jurisdiction (state board) so the exact combination varies by state [FACT — ADA licensure-for-international-dentists and licensure-by-state map]. conflict_axes.description: The default and reliable route is a CODA advanced-standing degree, but some states may accept a non-CODA degree or a credential route whose exact scope is unverified.
poles: bet on a non-CODA state route
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to CODA advanced standing and only pursue a non-CODA route after confirming that specific state board's current rule

conflict_axes.name: coda_credential_vs_direct_clinical_access
conflict_axes.description: Direct ADEX access requires a CODA/CDAC credential, so a foreign dentist without one cannot sit the clinical exam directly and depends on uncertain per-state permission.
poles: seek direct ADEX access without CODA
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sequence the CODA advanced-standing program first so it both satisfies the education gate and unlocks direct ADEX access

conflict_axes.name: cc_area_count_vs_scored_item_weight
conflict_axes.description: The number of CC areas in a group (13/23/20) and its share of scored items (~36/42/22%) describe different things and do not line up, inviting misallocated study time.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allocate study time by the scored-item weight (Group B highest) rather than by the raw count of CC areas

conflict_axes.name: estimate_band_vs_fabricated_precise_number
conflict_axes.description: Secondary sources offer precise-looking fees, retake intervals and pass rates that tempt fabricated certainty against the honest estimate/unknown posture.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry every unverified fee/interval/rate as a labeled estimate or unknown and require verification against a live official page before asserting it

conflict_axes.name: general_report_speed_vs_course_by_course_reuse
conflict_axes.description: A cheaper/faster ECE General Report suffices for exam eligibility but a Course-by-Course report is what advanced-standing programs need, so optimizing for exam speed can force a re-order.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: order the Course-by-Course report up front when advanced standing is the goal so one evaluation serves both eligibility and CAAPID

conflict_axes.name: single_synthesized_path_vs_atypical_state_route
conflict_axes.description: A single default sequence is clear and safe but can be sub-optimal for a candidate whose target state offers an atypical residency or non-CODA route.
poles: tailor to the target state's atypical route
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: follow the default sequence unless the target state's verified rules offer a faster residency or credential route worth tailoring to

edge_cases.description: A candidate assumes passing the INBDE alone grants a license and never plans for the separate clinical exam
edge_cases.trigger: the knowledge-only scope of the INBDE is overlooked
edge_cases.mitigation: state explicitly that the INBDE is knowledge-only and that ADEX/DLOSCE plus state licensure remain separate gates

edge_cases.description: A non-CODA graduate expects to sit ADEX directly without a CODA advanced-standing credential
edge_cases.trigger: the CODA-only direct-ADEX-access rule is not known
edge_cases.mitigation: route through a CODA advanced-standing program which unlocks direct ADEX access, or confirm a specific state board's permission route

edge_cases.description: A candidate orders only an ECE General Report then applies to advanced-standing programs that require Course-by-Course
edge_cases.trigger: the wrong ECE report type is chosen for the downstream goal
edge_cases.mitigation: order the Course-by-Course report up front when advanced standing is the goal so one evaluation serves eligibility and CAAPID

edge_cases.description: A downstream KB presents a complete numbered list of all 56 Clinical Content areas as official
edge_cases.trigger: the 403-blocked enumeration is reconstructed from partial snippets and treated as fact
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the 56-CC list marked UNKNOWN with only clearly-incomplete themes and verify against the Item Development Guide before enumerating

edge_cases.description: The secondary ~16.1% failure figure is quoted to a candidate as an official current pass statistic
edge_cases.trigger: an unverified secondary pass-rate number is asserted as fact
edge_cases.mitigation: state failures rose in direction after June 2024 while marking the exact rate UNKNOWN pending an official statistics release

edge_cases.description: A failer books a re-sit at 60 days when the current rule requires a longer interval and loses the slot
edge_cases.trigger: the estimate-tagged retake interval is treated as a confirmed current rule
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm the current interval and the 5-attempt/5-year caps in the live Candidate Guide before booking a re-sit

edge_cases.description: A candidate budgets a prior-year exam fee and is short at a non-refundable payment step
edge_cases.trigger: an estimate-tagged fee is treated as the fixed current fee
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the current ~$890 INBDE and ~$435 non-CODA fees on the live Apply page and treat them as non-refundable

edge_cases.description: A candidate misses the ADEA CAAPID March-January cycle and loses a full application year
edge_cases.trigger: the CAAPID cycle window is not tracked against the eligibility timeline
edge_cases.mitigation: align the DENTPIN/ECE evaluation timing so a Course-by-Course report is ready to submit within the CAAPID cycle

edge_cases.description: A candidate plans against a generic national checklist and misses their target state's jurisprudence exam or PGY-1 alternative
edge_cases.mitigation: resolve the target state's specific clinical-exam, jurisprudence and residency-alternative rules via the ADA licensure-by-state map

edge_cases.description: A candidate allocates study time by CC-area count and under-prepares the highest-item-weight group
edge_cases.trigger: the CC-area count is conflated with the scored-item weight
edge_cases.mitigation: allocate study by scored-item weight (Group B Oral Health Management ~42% highest) rather than by raw area count

edge_cases.description: A candidate studies from a commercial secondary guide treating it as an official blueprint authority
edge_cases.trigger: a secondary resource is mistaken for a primary JCNDE artifact while official PDFs are 403
edge_cases.mitigation: anchor on the JCNDE Candidate Guide and Item Development Guide as primary and use secondary guides only for orientation

edge_cases.description: A current (not-yet-graduated) non-CODA student omits the dean/registrar Certification of Eligibility and stalls eligibility
edge_cases.trigger: the student-specific certification step is skipped
edge_cases.mitigation: current students submit the dean/registrar Certification of Eligibility alongside the ECE evaluation as the Candidate Guide requires

workflow.action: Pin the exam identity and its knowledge-only scope
workflow.description: State INBDE = JCNDE/ADA knowledge exam replacing NBDE I/II (Aug 2020) and that it does not satisfy the clinical exam
workflow.gate: the identity, owner, replacement date and knowledge-only scope are stated with the Prometric/egress caveats tagged

workflow.description: Lay out education, credential-eval/exam and clinical gates and the per-state-board authority
workflow.gate: the three gates and the per-state-board variation are stated with owning nodes

workflow.action: Establish foreign-graduate INBDE eligibility and its step order
workflow.description: Require ECE evaluation + DENTPIN, choose the report type, and order the DENTPIN-first sequence
workflow.gate: ECE requirement, report-type choice and the DENTPIN -> JCNDE -> schedule sequence are stated with student-certification note

workflow.action: Specify the exam format and blueprint
workflow.description: Give the ~500-item 2-day structure and the 10 FK x 56 CC integrated matrix
workflow.gate: the item/day/timing structure and the FK x CC matrix are stated with the high-confidence-estimate tags

workflow.action: Enumerate FK areas and group the CC areas
workflow.description: List the 10 FK areas and the 3 CC groups with counts/weights, noting the count-vs-weight distinction
workflow.gate: all 10 FK areas and the 13/23/20 groups with ~36/42/22% weights are stated with estimate tags

workflow.description: Mark the full verbatim 56-area list UNKNOWN due to the 403/figure-image block and route it to verification
workflow.gate: the full 56-CC list is marked UNKNOWN with only incomplete themes and a fetch-enabled verification target

workflow.action: State the scoring, pass rule and its uncertainties
workflow.description: Give the 49-99 scale, 75 standard, pass/fail reporting, the June-2024 raise, and hold pass rates UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the scale, 75 standard and reporting are stated FACT and the current pass rate is held UNKNOWN

workflow.action: Give the retake policy and fees as labeled estimates
workflow.description: State the ~60-day interval and 5/5 caps and the ~$890/~$435 fees as estimates to verify
workflow.gate: the interval, caps and fees are tagged estimate/unknown with a verify-on-live-page flag

workflow.action: Solve the education gate via advanced standing and CAAPID
workflow.description: Require a CODA DDS/DMD via a ~2-3 year advanced-standing program applied to through ADEA CAAPID (March-January)
workflow.gate: the CODA-degree requirement, the advanced-standing program and the CAAPID cycle/report-type are stated

workflow.action: Name the clinical exam and resolve foreign access
workflow.description: Name ADEX/DLOSCE and state that only CODA/CDAC graduates take ADEX directly
workflow.gate: ADEX/DLOSCE, its administration and the CODA-only direct-access rule are stated

workflow.action: Resolve state licensure variation and its unknown routes
workflow.description: Use the ADA state map as authority and hold the exact non-CODA-friendly state list UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the state-board authority and varying requirements are stated with the non-CODA state list held UNKNOWN

workflow.action: Compose the end-to-end path with its named blockers
workflow.description: Order ECE/DENTPIN -> INBDE(75) -> CAAPID -> advanced standing -> ADEX/DLOSCE -> state licensure and list the UNKNOWN blockers
workflow.gate: the ordered path is composed and the fee/retake/pass-rate/56-CC/non-CODA-state blockers are listed as to-verify not asserted

priority_rationale: The exam identity and the three-gate pathway come first because every other node hangs on knowing what the INBDE is and where it sits among the education, exam and clinical gates; foreign-graduate eligibility (ECE + DENTPIN) and the exam format/blueprint/scoring nodes come next because they specify the exam gate a candidate must clear; the named UNKNOWN blockers (56-CC enumeration, current pass rate, retake interval, fees, non-CODA state list) attach to their parent nodes so no fabricated number propagates; the education-gate (CODA advanced standing + CAAPID) and the clinical-gate (ADEX/DLOSCE + foreign access) then build the surrounding pathway; and the state-variation and end-to-end synthesis come last because they compose every upstream gate and blocker into an ordered, honestly-caveated licensure path.

dominance_rules.rule: The knowledge-only scope of the INBDE dominates any assumption it yields a license
dominance_rules.rationale: the INBDE does not satisfy the separate clinical exam or state licensure
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan treats passing the INBDE as sufficient for licensure
dominance_rules.action: reassert that ADEX/DLOSCE and state licensure remain separate gates after the INBDE

dominance_rules.rule: The specific state board dominates any generic national checklist
dominance_rules.rationale: licensure requirements are set per jurisdiction and vary widely
dominance_rules.trigger: a requirement is planned against a national rulebook
dominance_rules.action: resolve it against the target state board via the ADA licensure-by-state map

dominance_rules.rule: The CODA credential dominates the direct-clinical-access question
dominance_rules.rationale: only CODA/CDAC graduates may take ADEX directly
dominance_rules.trigger: a foreign graduate expects direct ADEX access without a CODA degree
dominance_rules.action: route through a CODA advanced-standing program or confirm a specific state board's permission route

dominance_rules.rule: The labeled estimate/unknown dominates any precise-looking secondary number
dominance_rules.rationale: fees, retake intervals and pass rates come from secondary snippets, not directly-read official pages
dominance_rules.trigger: a fee, interval or pass rate is about to be stated as fact
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate/unknown and require verification against a live official page before asserting it

dominance_rules.rule: The UNKNOWN marker dominates the 56-CC enumeration
dominance_rules.rationale: the official list is 403-blocked and only partial themes are corroborated
dominance_rules.trigger: a complete or numbered 56-CC list is about to be presented
dominance_rules.action: mark it UNKNOWN, keep only clearly-incomplete themes, and route to Item Development Guide verification

dominance_rules.rule: The scored-item weight dominates the CC-area count for study allocation
dominance_rules.rationale: area counts and item-weight shares describe different things and do not line up
dominance_rules.trigger: study time is being allocated by number of CC areas
dominance_rules.action: allocate by scored-item weight, with Group B (Oral Health Management ~42%) highest

dominance_rules.rule: The Course-by-Course report dominates the General Report when advanced standing is the goal
dominance_rules.rationale: programs and CAAPID require Course-by-Course, so a General Report forces a re-order
dominance_rules.trigger: an ECE report type is chosen while advanced standing is intended
dominance_rules.action: order the Course-by-Course report up front so one evaluation serves eligibility and CAAPID

dominance_rules.rule: The primary JCNDE artifacts dominate any commercial secondary guide
dominance_rules.rationale: only the Candidate Guide, Item Development Guide and Domain model are authoritative
dominance_rules.trigger: a secondary guide is used as a blueprint authority
dominance_rules.action: anchor on the primary JCNDE artifacts and use secondary guides only for orientation

dominance_rules.rule: Adequate first-attempt preparation dominates reliance on retakes
dominance_rules.rationale: the raised standard and limited 5-attempt/5-year envelope penalize avoidable retakes
dominance_rules.trigger: an exam plan leans on retaking rather than clearing 75 first time
dominance_rules.action: prepare to the absolute 75 bar before the first sitting to preserve the retake envelope

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the ECE Course-by-Course report up front when advanced standing is the goal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a second, later Course-by-Course order and a lost CAAPID cycle after a General Report was bought

anti_rework_rules.rule: Secure a DENTPIN before ordering the ECE evaluation or attempting to schedule
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a paid evaluation or a scheduling attempt stalling for lack of an ID

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the current retake interval and attempt/time caps before booking a re-sit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mis-timed re-sit booking lost to a changed interval

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the current fees on the live Apply page before making a non-refundable payment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a budgeting shortfall or forfeiture at a non-refundable fee step

anti_rework_rules.rule: Align the eligibility timeline to the ADEA CAAPID March-January cycle
anti_rework_rules.prevents: missing the CAAPID window and losing a full application year

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve the target state board's specific requirements before finalizing the plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering a missed state jurisprudence exam or PGY-1 alternative late in the process

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark the 56-CC enumeration and current pass rate UNKNOWN when first drafting content
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a downstream KB propagating a fabricated official 56-area list or pass statistic that must be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Sequence the CODA advanced-standing program before planning the clinical exam
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a candidate passing the INBDE but being unable to sit ADEX for lack of a CODA credential
